summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: Student Backpack Production (Part 1) ## Introduction Hi, welcome to Marvelous Designer's asset creation tutorial. In this tutorial, we will make a student backpack. ## Loading the Model First, we will load a virtual model from the library window and use it to determine the size of the backpack. Download our default T-shirt and pants, select the automatically adjusted version, and start making the backpack after the version is automatically modified. ## Setting Up the Workspace 1. Move all the versions in the 2D window to the side. 2. Select the rectangular tool and create half of the version based on the model screenshot in the 2D window. 3. In the tool group in the Edit tab, select the vertical point in the lower right corner of the original version and drag it to make it a rectangle. ## Dividing the Rectangle 1. In the tool group in the Edit tab, find the plus point division tool on the top right of the line and open the partition window. 2. In the window, select an average segment with a number of lines set to 4, then click OK to see three dots. 3. Switch to the Edit panel tool, right-click on the newly created point, and choose to convert it to a free curve point. 4. Select the middle line, right-click, and select Open. ## Positioning the Panels 1. In the 3D window, select the panel and use the positioning ball to place it behind the model. 2. Use the Edit panel tool to select the middle panel, right-click, and select Copy. Then, right-click on the appropriate position and select Paste to copy a similar panel. 3. Select the previous panel, right-click, and select Level Rotate to turn it over. Then right-click again and select Freeze Panel. ## Finalizing Panel Arrangement 1. Use the positioning ball to copy and paste the selected panel behind the model. 2. Select the free curve tool to create a seam line between the two panels. 3. Press the control grid key on the keyboard to run the simulation. The panel on the inside will be fixed in 3D space as a basis for fixing other panels. ## Editing and Adjusting Panels 1. Use the delete button to delete the extra straight lines from the arrangement panel to add a cutting edge to the panel. 2. Use the delete tool to find the long edge at the bottom of the panel. 3. Press the Q key to enter from the male number 3, tpaw 1, with the height of the panel set to 110. ## Adjusting Panel Width and Length 1. Use Shift to select curving stitches on the lower shell, and adjust the length accordingly. 2. Use the table to locate where the width of the panel was set, then find the corresponding length. 3. Raise each element to match the center line. ## Positioning Newly Created Panels Next, we will adjust the position of the panels in the 2D window. Select the two panels that have been newly created and move them to the right position in the 3D window. Click on the panel, follow the position of the 3D window, and use the positioning ball to rotate it to the right position. Please note that the panels should be facing inward. ## Sewing the Panels 1. Select the free sewing tool to create a sewing line between the side panels and the backpack panels. 2. Sew while observing the sewing line in the 3D window to ensure that the sewing line is in the right direction. 3. Select the panel you just frozen, right-click, select Copy and Paste, and copy a similar panel. ## Creating the Front of the Bag This panel will become the front of the bag, so I need to untangle it. Then, use the free sewing tool to sew it together with the side panels. When all panels are combined, use the adjustment panel tool to select all the bag panels, right-click, select Hardening, then press the control button to start modeling. ## Pressure Adjustment 1. Select all panels other than the frozen panels, and then select the panel you just frozen. 2. In the attribute editor, change their pressure to 1, and then start modeling. The bag will bulge, and this step is complete. ## Creating the Side Pocket Now we will create the pocket on the side of the bag. 1. Select the Edit panel tool and press the Shift key to select the two sides of the side panel. 2. To create an internal line according to the value you entered, preview the position of the internal line (for example, 180mm). 3. After confirmation, right-click on the internal line created and choose to cut and sew. ## Building the Pocket Board 1. Use the adjustment board tool to select the next small board and copy and paste a board. 2. Place the created pocket board in the 3D window to the corresponding position of the pocket. 3. Use the Edit board tool to select the line at the top and move it so that the pocket board becomes wider. ## Adjusting Pocket Dimensions 1. Select this line on the left and press the right arrow key on the keyboard to move it 10mm to reduce the height of the pocket board. 2. Select the border of the two sides and bottom of the pocket, right-click, and select the expansion of the pocket board. Set the diameter to 20mm and select the corner as the side angle. 3. Select the extra point and press the delete key to delete it. ## Sewing the Pocket Board 1. Use the free sewing tool to sew the pocket board to the side panel. 2. After sewing the other lines one by one, please pay attention to the side sewing line of the pocket. Sew to the blue reference point, which is the equal length position. ## Creating the Pocket Fold To create the fold of the top of the pocket, use the Edit board tool. Select the line on the left, right-click, and select the internal line diameter to set the diameter to 20mm. Create a new line in the element editor on the right, selecting the flexible option. Set the flexible ratio to 50 for the outer line of the tablet and set the same value. ## Simulation and Adjustment 1. Use the Edit board tool to select the board, press the button to print, then press the control button to start the simulation. 2. After the simulation is stable, press the button to remove the print. 3. In the element editor, reduce the particle diameter from 20 to 10, then simulate again, and repeat until reduced to 5. ## Increasing Visual Thickness In the element editor, increase the thickness of the reference to enhance visual thickness. Adjust the pressure of the pocket panel to 0. If you need to check the thickness, please open the density pattern surface in the try to display menu. ## Creating a Mirror Pocket If you want to create the same pocket on the other side, use the Edit board tool to select the pocket panel. Then select the copy option in the menu bar on the right and choose the mirror paste option to create a mirror image. ## Final Adjustments 1. Similarly, use the free sewing tool to complete the sewing line. 2. Select the version and press the right button to print and then simulate. After confirming that the versions are all sewed together, use the Edit version tool to select one of the internal lines and then press the right button to cut the seam allowance. ## Conclusion Open the simulation and confirm that the two pockets have been adjusted. In the next parts of this tutorial, we will continue to refine the backpack and add additional details. ```
